response.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT ID, AVG(PIC) AS avg_pic, AVG(HGB) * 1.0 / NULLIF(AVG(HCT), 0) AS ratio FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID), m AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS mean_ratio FROM p WHERE ratio IS NOT NULL) SELECT AVG(p.avg_pic) AS mean_avg_pic, AVG(p.ratio) AS mean_ratio, AVG(p.ratio - m.mean_ratio) AS mean_ratio_diff FROM p CROSS JOIN m WHERE p.ratio > m.mean_ratio;

assumptions.assumption: A patient's hemoglobin-to-hematocrit ratio is AVG(HGB) divided by AVG(HCT) over all of their lab records, with NULLs ignored by AVG.
Patients with no computable ratio (no HGB or HCT values, or average HCT of 0) are excluded from the all-patient mean ratio and cannot be kept.
Kept patients with no PIC values have a NULL average PIC, which is ignored in the mean of average PIC values.

alternatives.interpretation: The patient's ratio is the average of the per-record ratios HGB/HCT, using only records where both values are present.
